To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) binary segmentation of humans in video sequences can be used as a preprocessing step for human detection; (2) multi label segmentation of humans in images is a challenging task that can be solved by means of a multi class conditional random field approach; (3) human pose estimation can be improved by means of poselets and the use of depth data is beneficial; and (4) gesture recognition can be done by using a bag of words representation of RGB and depth data
1. Binary segmentation of the human body can be used to improve the performance of other human analysis algorithms.
1) Graph cuts optimization is a suitable framework for human segmentation, providing good segmentation results and allowing to remove background clutter in image sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the visual analysis of human body in image and video sequences.
the problem of human visual analysis, which is a topic of interest due the relevance of humans for many computer vision applications.
learning visual representations of the humans body that are helpful to the analysis of humans in video sequences, from the raw pixels of an image to the final gesture that is performed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in this thesis we present a framework that is able to learn different visual representations of humans from images and video sequences that are helpful for visual human analysis in both RGB and depth modalities.
the visual analysis of human body from images and video sequences is a very interesting and challenging problem.

we have shown that it is possible to learn visual representations of the body from RGB and depth image data, at three different levels of abstraction, from pixels to gestures, that are useful for the visual analysis and interpretation of human body in image data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present novel approaches for the visual analysis in color and/or depth data sequences, that are able to deal with the challenging problem of the analysis of humans in video sequences, and that can be used in different applications like pedestrian detection, surveillance, human computer interfaces, or content based retrieval, among others.
we present a set of methods that can be useful to the computer vision community in the analysis of humans from RGB and depth images.
we have presented a framework for learning different visual representations for human visual analysis in color and RGBD data sequences, at different levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although we are still far from the goal of fully automatic visual human analysis, the combination of the presented methods can be used to achieve state of the art results in several tasks related to visual human analysis.

, in general, the use of multiple visual representations of the humans in images and videos, at different levels, can be very helpful in order to improve the performance of the visual analysis methods.
the combination of different image modalities, as well as the use of different visual representations, can yield to better results in the context of human visual analysis.
